mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A low-topped miniature supercell over central OH may continue for another hour or two this evening. A brief tornado remains possible. A Watch is currently not expected

details.label: Summary
details.text: A low-topped miniature supercell over central OH may continue for another hour or two this evening. A brief tornado remains possible. A Watch is currently not expected

details.label: Discussion
details.text: As of 0120 UTC, the Dayton, OH TDWR and KILN NEXRAD showed a miniature supercell over Champaign County, OH. This storm is ongoing within a broader cluster of low-topped convection near a remnant MCV across central OH. The environment is not particularly unstable (MLCAPE 500-1000 J/kg), but is very moist, with dewpoints in the mid 70s F. This is supporting low cloud bases amid enlarged low-level hodographs ahead of the MCV. SPC mesoanalysis shows ESRH of 100-200 m2/s2 across central OH which could support occasional low-level rotation despite much weaker deep-layer shear. This storm has displayed intermittent low-level mesocyclones and potentially produced a brief tornado earlier this evening from public reports. The modestly supportive environment and cellular storm mode suggest a brief tornado or two will remain possible as the storm moves eastward over the next couple of hours. However, the lack of stronger deep-layer shear and weak buoyancy favor only intermittent intensification. Increasing inhibition is also expected to slowly diminish the threat later this evening. Given the brief and localized nature of the threat, a Watch is not anticipated
